title: Exact Low-Length Recht–Ré Inequalities and Metric-Dependent Rankings in Random Reshuffling Dynamics
shortTitle: Exact Recht–Ré inequalities and sampling dynamics
oneLine: An exact low-length matrix-inequality classification becomes a metric-aware theory of data ordering: mean iterates, quadratic risk, fresh reshuffling, single shuffle and replica averaging can rank the same sampler differently.
abstract: This combined unrefereed candidate contains two linked manuscripts. The first gives an exact computer-assisted classification of the Recht–Ré matrix inequality through five factors and proves balanced six-factor families. The second develops a metric-aware operator framework for random reshuffling, with exact rational examples in which a first-moment proxy ranks sampling without replacement worse while the Gram operator ranks it better. On the certified five-factor family it proves fresh-reshuffling Gram dominance for every positive epoch count, an exact replica crossover, endpoint and nearby all-horizon single-shuffle dominance, exact two- and three-epoch stepsize transitions, rational simplex families, and a perturbation radius. The package passed a clean-extraction exact replay with fail-closed verifiers and mutation controls. It has not received an unaffiliated rerun, independent reimplementation, proof-assistant verification, specialist acceptance or editorial peer review.
narration: When is one data-ordering scheme better than another? This release shows that the answer depends on the mathematical quantity being compared. Its first paper gives an exact computer-assisted classification of the Recht–Ré matrix inequality through five factors, plus balanced six-factor families. Its second paper follows one rational counterexample into repeated optimisation dynamics. There, reshuffling can have a worse mean iterate but a better expected squared error. Fresh reshuffling beats with-replacement sampling in the certified invariant Gram channel at every positive epoch count. Reusing one permutation, called single shuffle, agrees with fresh reshuffling after one epoch but is strictly better at every later epoch at the endpoint, with exact phase transitions away from it. Averaging independent runs introduces a separate bias–variance crossover at one hundred and forty-five over seven. These are exact, family-specific and metric-specific statements, not a universal ranking of optimisation algorithms. The public archive includes both papers, exact rational certificates, separate internal verifiers, mutation controls, manifests, checksums and a clean-extraction replay receipt. Those checks establish artifact identity and producer-side internal replay. They do not establish independent reproduction, formal verification, specialist acceptance, peer review, novelty priority or real-world performance.

problem.name: Metric-aware comparison of random reshuffling, with-replacement sampling and single shuffle

keyResults: Four factors: the two-sided Recht–Ré inequality holds for every n ≥ 4.
Five factors: the upper bound holds for every n ≥ 5; the lower bound fails sharply at n = 5 and is restored for every n ≥ 6.
Six factors: the upper bound holds when 7 divides n, the lower bound when 8 divides n, and the two-sided inequality when 56 divides n; other cases remain open.

On the certified five-factor family, the first-moment ranking reverses the invariant Gram ranking, and fresh reshuffling has the smaller Gram channel than with-replacement sampling for every positive epoch count.
At the endpoint, single shuffle equals fresh reshuffling at one epoch and is strictly Loewner-below it for every K ≥ 2; one uniform open stepsize neighbourhood preserves the all-horizon ranking.

Replica averaging has an exact crossover at r* = 145/7 on the all-ones direction; the K = 2 and K = 3 single-shuffle comparisons have exact interior stepsize transitions near 0.815893501141 and 0.788002536290.
Exact rational reversal families hold for full reshuffling at (n,k) = (5,5) and (6,6), and for the six-step without-replacement prefix at (7,6); this last protocol is not a full epoch.

openProblems: Classify arbitrary quadratic objectives by deciding block positivity of the endpoint Choi/Gram difference, or produce an exact rational product-vector counterexample.
Determine whether the regular-simplex Gram dominance extends to all lengths; exact checks through length 19 are evidence for a conjecture, not a proof.
Find conditioning radii under which metric-specific Gram order is uniform in dimension and horizon, or construct the smallest near-identity Gram reversal.
Extend the symmetry-channel comparison to commutants with multiplicity, where invariant positive forms are matrix blocks rather than a simplicial cone.
Complete the six-factor Recht–Ré classification outside the certified divisibility families and seek conceptual proofs for the exact certificate results.
Obtain an unaffiliated clean-archive rerun, a clean-room implementation of the theorem-to-encoding bridge, proof-assistant formalisation, and verified specialist review.
